answer: Each identity anchors to a river segment and locks a 60-credit bond. One ridge station serves a segment and holds 10 identities; its opener pays its cost. Stations follow a spiral transect from ridge crest to river mouth, so station j costs 400+20(j-1) credits. For 1,000 fakes, 100 stations cost 139,000, bonds lock 60,000, 10-credit fees add 10,000, totaling 209,000. A station-sharing ring fails: a full station rejects an eleventh identity and burns its bond. Any auditor can recount stations from the river ledger. An honest agent joins one station once, pays one fee, and keeps its bond.
